# S15 — Build the web viewer

A replay-only web viewer in `web/`: plain JavaScript ES modules with JSDoc types and canvas, no framework, no build step, that plays replay files with step, play, pause and seek and matches the terminal viewer's frame model on the shared fixture.

**Findings:** PROJECT.md Milestone 7, Goals 6 · **Size:** L · **Tree:** web
Cites: C06 goal: Terminal and web visualizer of recorded replays, C19 requirement: Terminal and web viewers play the same replay file correctly, C13 constraint: Every dependency needs owner approval, C28 decision: Core language: Go standard library only; plain JS + canvas web viewer, C31 decision: Visualizer priority: terminal viewer first, web viewer second, C35 constraint: Implementer decides unfixed interface details and records them

**Not in this slice:** hosting (later tier, S20); live matches through WASM (optional S14); TypeScript or `tsc` (needs separate owner approval, C28); any JS package, bundler or test framework (C13).

## Why

v1 feature list, goal 6 and acceptance criterion C19: the terminal and web viewers both play the same replay file correctly. C31 puts it after the terminal viewer, whose fixture (`testdata/viewer/`) it reuses. A replay-only viewer needs no WASM (C28).

## Files

- `web/index.html`, `web/style.css`.
- `web/js/replay.js` (parse the JSON-lines replay per `docs/spec/replay.md`), `web/js/model.js` (frame model), `web/js/player.js` (step, play, pause, seek), `web/js/render.js` (canvas), `web/js/main.js` (wiring; replay chosen with a file input).
- `web/test/harness.js`: a tiny in-repo test harness (test registration, deep-equal assert, results list); `web/test/*.test.js`; `web/test.html` runs them and shows pass/fail.
- A local static server for `web/` and `testdata/viewer/`, since browsers block `fetch` from `file://`: the smallest stdlib option, for example a `pit serve` subcommand on 127.0.0.1 using `net/http`, with a Go test using `net/http/httptest`. The implementer decides and records it per C35. S14 reuses it.
- `AGENTS.md`: how to serve and run the web tests.

## Failing tests

- `replay.test.js`: parsing `testdata/viewer/fixture.jsonl` gives the expected header and event counts; an unknown version is rejected.
- `model.test.js`: the frame model at each sampled cycle equals `testdata/viewer/frames.json` (the same expectation the terminal viewer's `TestFrames` uses).
- `player.test.js`: seeking to cycle N equals stepping N times; table-driven state machine transitions.
- Go: the serve command's test (if added) serves a file from a `t.TempDir()` and refuses paths outside its root.

## Implement

- Every JS file starts with `// @ts-check` and uses JSDoc types for editor checking only; no `tsc` run, no `package.json`.
- Keep parsing, model and player free of DOM access so the tests can run them directly; only `render.js` and `main.js` touch the DOM and canvas.
- Canvas drawing of cell ownership (color per bot from last-writer id) and execution pointers; the layout and colors are the implementer's call, recorded per C35.

## Check

- `. scripts/env.sh && go test ./... && go vet ./... && test -z "$(gofmt -l cmd internal)"` passes.
- Manual: serve the files, open `web/test.html`; every test passes.
- Manual: open `web/index.html`, load `internal/replay/testdata/imp_dwarf_seed1.jsonl`, and step, play, pause and seek.
- Owner input, optional: automated JS tests in a terminal (`node --test`, Node is installed here) need owner approval of Node as a toolchain (C13). Without it, the browser test page is the check.

## Git

Branch `slice/<id>-web-viewer` in `.worktrees/<id>`. One commit when the owner asks.
